artifacts.summary: Traces the vendor hook-recurrence mechanism, confirms live capture/activation coupling asymmetry, finds abood's unmerged-hook-fragment signal, designs the N-repeat agreement rule, and scopes the two doc rewrites for the five dispatched GOAL items.

memory_candidates.content: Sapience vendor client (~/.sapience/sapience_upkeep.py) re-adds three Claude Code hooks (SessionStart --briefing-text, SessionEnd --receipt, Stop --effect-line) to $HOME/.claude/settings.json unconditionally on every auto_update/update --wire pass, UNLESS ~/.sapience/config.json's "hooks" key is false or SAPIENCE_NO_HOOKS=1 is set (hooks_opted_out()). This is independent of any repository's own sapience extension load state -- a machine-wide recurrence risk any verifier for this extension should check.

Sapience transcript capture is gated by a SEPARATE opt-in list, ~/.sapience/config.json's capture.projects[].enabled (matched by longest path_prefix, mirroring sapience_capture.py's for_cwd()), unconnected to a repository's own sapience extension activation state (.claude-extensions.json's extensions.sapience.status). A repository can be active-extension with capture disabled/absent (observed: BimodalLogic, Sapience/sf1-engine) or, in principle, capture-enabled with the extension inactive (not observed but possible) -- no existing script in the extension's source store reads or writes this list.
